newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Vereinsbank chief downplays risks of takeover.
newsitem.headline: Vereinsbank chief downplays risks of takeover.

text.p: The head of Germany's Bayerische Vereinsbank AG, a bank often cited as a takoever target, on Tuesday downplayed the likelihood it might be the object of a hostile bid.
Albrecht Schmidt, chief executive of Germany's fifth largest bank, told Reuters there was a need for change in the overcrowded German banking landscape, but said hostile takeovers would not work.
Nor was Vereinsbank itself actively on the lookout for a major takeover, Schmidt said, in an interview on the fringes of the International Monetary Conference in Switzerland.
"The profile of the bank is far more important than its size," he said.

Vereinsbank has been at the centre of merger speculation in Germany since last July when market leader Deutsche Bank AG revealed it had built up a 5.21 percent stake in the Bavarian mortgage lending specialist.
"Deutsche threw its hat in the ring," Schmidt conceded.
But for a merger to work in Germany, extensive preparation had to be done and the participants in the alliance would have to match in terms of corporate culture.
"It makes no sense to become larger and weaker," Schmidt said.
Schmidt cited ABN-AMRO in the Netherlands and Chase Manhattan Corp in the U.S. as examples of how bank mergers could actually work.
But he said Vereinsbank's focus would be on maximising productivity and expanding key business areas.
On personnel, Schmidt said he did not envisage major staff cuts, but rather expected employees to be flexible.
"Cutting staff is not a dominant topic for us," he said.
